newsitem.title: UK: Hyder says windfall tax needn't hit strategy.
newsitem.headline: Hyder says windfall tax needn't hit strategy.

text.p: British water and electricity company Hyder Plc would not change strategy if a one-off "windfall" tax proposed by the new Labour government was at a "reasonable" level, finance director Paul Twamley told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"If we had a figure which was very, very silly, then obviously we would have to look again, but if there is any reasonable level of apportionment...we think it should not, would not change our strategy," he said.

The government, which rolled into power with a huge majority on May 1, has vowed to introduce a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities as a central plank of its first budget, to be announced on July 2.
Twamley said the 11-percent real growth in total dividend to 43.9 pence per share was declared "knowing that there is going to be a windfall tax...we have to take that into account in what we do."
Twamley said Hyder was not calculating on a specific level for the proposed tax but considering a range of possibilities.
"You have to try and guess...half a dozen levels of windfall tax...You can't have a number...because we don't even know the basis yet leave alone who's going to be included," he said.
